writtenAt: 2026-10-12 (before any evaluation; probed that day against the local container with self-registered customers: transfer, bill payment, account transactions and every search variant with curl, directly under /services/bank and through the pages' own /services_proxy/bank with a session cookie, and the Transfer Funds, Bill Pay, Find Transactions, Account Activity, Transaction Details and Accounts Overview pages in a browser running in the America/New_York time zone; every keyed defect reproduced at least twice with a control case that behaves correctly)
format: a loose product-owner story, eight bullets and a refinement note, no numbered criteria, web pages and API together; AC-1 to AC-8 below are the bullets in the story's order (1 transfer and balances, 2 history on both accounts with amount and date, 3 what a valid amount is, 4 never more than the account holds, 5 two different accounts, 6 bill payment and its payee details, 7 find transactions, 8 only one's own accounts). The checks need a data chain: a registered customer, a second account opened from the first, a transfer or payment, the entries on both accounts, then the searches; AC-8 needs a second registered customer

defects.description: bullet 4 (never more than the account holds), transfers: a transfer larger than the sending account's balance is carried out. API: with 115.75 on the account, POST /services/bank/transfer?fromAccountId={b}&toAccountId={a}&amount=500 answers 200 "Successfully transferred $500 ..." and the account reads -384.25; a second time with amount=115.76 (one cent too much). Web: Transfer Funds of 9000 from an account holding $113.20 shows "Transfer Complete!" and the overview lists -$8886.80. Control: 15.75 from an account holding 415.50 moves exactly 15.75. The story requires a refusal and unchanged balances

bullet 3 (a valid amount), transfers: a negative amount is accepted and moves the money the other way. API: POST transfer?fromAccountId={a}&toAccountId={b}&amount=-20 answers 200 "Successfully transferred $-20", a goes up by 20.00 and b down by 20.00, and both histories get an entry with amount -20.00 (again with -0.01). Web: amount -7 shows "Transfer Complete! -$7.00 has been transferred" and the balances move the wrong way. Control: 15.75 moves 15.75 from a to b. The story requires that no money moves, no entry is written and the customer is told what is wrong

bullet 3, transfers: a transfer of zero is accepted. POST transfer?...&amount=0 (and amount=0.00) answers 200 "Successfully transferred $0" and writes a "Funds Transfer Sent" 0.00 entry on the sending account and a "Funds Transfer Received" 0.00 entry on the receiving one; balances are unchanged. The story requires a refusal with no entry in the history

bullet 5 (two different accounts): a transfer from an account to the same account is accepted. API: POST transfer?fromAccountId={a}&toAccountId={a}&amount=10 answers 200 and the account gets two entries (10.00 sent, 10.00 received), balance unchanged; repeated on a second account. Web: choosing the same account in both lists shows "Transfer Complete! $3.00 has been transferred from account #X to account #X". The story requires two different accounts

bullet 3, fractions of a cent: an amount with three decimals is accepted, and afterwards both accounts can no longer be read. POST transfer?fromAccountId={a}&toAccountId={b}&amount=2.345 answers 200 "Successfully transferred $2.345"; from then on GET accounts/{a}, accounts/{b}, accounts/{a}/transactions and customers/{c}/accounts answer 500 with the site's HTML error page (server log: ArithmeticException "Rounding necessary"), the customer's Accounts Overview shows "An internal error has occurred", and any further transfer from these accounts answers 500. Reproduced with two customers (1.005 and 2.345); control: 1.05 on the same accounts just before is carried out and read back correctly, and a third account of the same customer stays readable. The story requires that such an amount moves no money

bullet 3, the customer is told what is wrong: on the Transfer Funds page, submitting with the amount left empty, or with text ("abc"), shows the page "Error! An internal error has occurred and has been logged." and nothing about the amount (the page holds the texts "The amount cannot be empty." and "Please enter a valid amount." but never shows them). No money moves. In the API the same inputs answer 500 with the HTML error page (amount empty or missing) and 404 with an empty body (amount=abc). Control: the Bill Pay page shows "The amount cannot be empty." and "Please enter a valid amount." next to the field for the same inputs

bullet 4, bill payments: a payment larger than the account's balance is made. API: with 455.10 on the account, POST /services/bank/billpay?accountId={a}&amount=600 with a complete payee answers 200 and the account reads -144.90 (also 5000 from 325.49). Web: Bill Pay of 5000 from an account holding $100.00 shows "Bill Payment Complete" and the overview lists -$4900.00; again 150 from $100.00 gives -$50.00. Control: 60.40 from 515.50 leaves 455.10. The story requires a refusal and unchanged balances

bullet 3, bill payments: a negative or zero payment amount is accepted. API: billpay?accountId={a}&amount=-30 answers 200 {"amount":-30} and the account goes UP by 30.00, with a "Bill Payment to ..." entry of -30.00; amount=0 answers 200 and writes a 0.00 entry. Web: amount -12 shows "Bill Payment Complete ... in the amount of $-12.00" and the account rises by 12.00; amount 0 shows "Bill Payment Complete". Control: text in the amount is refused on the page with "Please enter a valid amount."

bullet 6 (all payee details are required): the API makes a payment without them. POST billpay?accountId={a}&amount=1 with the body {} answers 200 {"payeeName":null,...}, debits 1.00 and writes the entry "Bill Payment to null"; with empty strings in every payee field it writes "Bill Payment to "; with only a name it pays as well. Control: the Bill Pay page refuses the empty form with a message at each field ("Payee name is required." and so on) and a mismatch of the two account numbers with "The account numbers do not match."

bullet 2 (the date the transfer was made): the Account Activity page and the Find Transactions results show an entry one day too early. A transfer made on 10-12-2026 is listed as 10-11-2026 on activity.htm and in every Find Transactions result, while the Transaction Details page of the same entry shows 10-12-2026, the API gives 2026-10-12 00:00 UTC, and searching by the date 10-12-2026 finds the entry (shown as 10-11-2026) while 10-11-2026 finds nothing. Cause: the pages format the API's midnight-UTC date in the browser's local time. Seen on every entry in a browser in America/New_York; it shows in any browser whose time zone is west of UTC, at the times of day when the local date equals the server's (UTC) date, and does not show in a browser at UTC or east of it. An evaluation whose browser runs at UTC or east cannot see it

bullet 8 (only one's own accounts): a customer can move money out of another customer's account and read its history, and so can somebody who is not signed in. Signed in as customer B (session cookie, through /services_proxy/bank): POST transfer?fromAccountId={account of A}&toAccountId={account of B}&amount=50 answers 200, A is 50.00 lower and B 50.00 higher; POST billpay?accountId={account of A}&amount=11 pays from A's account; GET accounts/{account of A} and accounts/{account of A}/transactions/amount/50 answer 200 with A's data. Directly under /services/bank the same calls answer 200 with no cookie and no credentials at all (transfer of 25 out of A's account). Control: through /services_proxy/bank without a session cookie the transfer answers 401 {"message":"User login required"}. The Transaction Details page (transaction.htm?id=N) also shows any customer's entry to a visitor who is not signed in

traps: D5 destroys the accounts it touches: after a three-decimal transfer both accounts, the customer's account list and their overview answer 500 for good (nothing in the application repairs it, and the admin page and the clean/initialize functions are off limits). The test for it needs its own freshly registered customer, and must be the last thing done with those accounts
the tests for D1, D2, D7, D8 and D11 leave balances changed or negative: every test that asserts balances needs customers and accounts of its own, registered in that test
D10 depends on the time zone of the browser (and the hour): see its description. The search by date itself is correct on the server; only the date shown is shifted

Find Transactions works as the story asks: by id, by date (MM-DD-YYYY), by date range (both ends included) and by exact amount, the matching entries and no others, and an empty table for no match. An unknown transaction id answers 400 "Could not find transaction #N" in the API and an empty result on the page. No finding there

the page's search by transaction id ignores the chosen account (it asks for the transaction alone): with an id of another account of the same customer it shows that entry. The story does not say the id search is limited to the selected account; ids of another customer's entries fall under D11

the API accepts a transfer whose receiving account belongs to another customer; the page offers only the customer's own accounts as destination. The story is about transfers between one's own accounts and does not say whether paying into someone else's account is forbidden: a question for the owner. Moving money OUT of someone else's account is D11
the payee's account number is not checked against anything (the payee is outside the bank): not a defect. The page requires the phone number, as the story does

an account that does not exist is refused correctly: transfer answers 400 "Could not find account number X and/or Y", GET accounts/{id} and its transactions answer 400 with a message; bill payment from an account that does not exist answers 500 with the HTML error page, which the story does not cover (no criterion on unknown accounts)
an amount with one decimal (12.5) is valid and is stored as 12.50; the API's confirmation text echoes the amount as typed ("$12.5", "$-20")

the transfer API answers plain text, the bill payment API answers JSON and wants the payee as a JSON body with accountId and amount as query parameters; without "Accept: application/json" answers are XML; dates in the API are epoch milliseconds at midnight UTC

the pages are shells that load and send through /parabank/services_proxy/bank/... with the session cookie (401 without one), while /parabank/services/bank/... needs no credentials: a test that only tries the proxy path without a cookie sees a correct 401 and misses the anonymous half of D11

a second account for the chain comes from Open New Account and costs 100.00 of the first account's 515.50 (both figures are settings of this installation); the opening itself writes a "Funds Transfer Sent"/"Funds Transfer Received" entry of 100.00 on the two accounts, which a search by amount or date will also return
the Transfer Funds page fills both account lists with a call made after the page has loaded; a test must wait for the options
